claim: A man crucified in Roman Judea could be taken down and buried in a family tomb.

bible.note: Joseph of Arimathea asks Pilate for Jesus's body and lays it in a rock-cut tomb before the Sabbath.
The Jewish law that a hanged man's body must not remain overnight but be buried the same day.

outside.source: The heel bone of Yehohanan, Giv'at ha-Mivtar, Jerusalem
outside.note: A family tomb held an ossuary inscribed 'Yehohanan son of Hagkol' containing a right heel bone still pierced by an iron nail, with wood attached. The nail had bent, so it could not be removed. This is physical evidence of a crucified man whose bones were collected and placed in his family's tomb.
Says Jews were so careful about burial that they took down even those condemned to crucifixion and buried them before sunset.

counter: Romans often left crucified bodies on the cross to rot or for animals, as a deterrent, and some scholars (such as John Dominic Crossan) argue Jesus was most likely not given a proper burial. Yehohanan is a single case and his circumstances are unknown; the details of how he was crucified have been re-examined and are still debated. This shows burial was possible, not that it happened to Jesus.
